done.why: I died three times at the Guardians, and the old man told me he probably didn't have a fourth revival in him. The mirror box was left in front of the statues and I couldn't get back inside it. In the past, the jewel room was locked from the inside. The Royal Puzzle's own note warns you can get trapped in there. On my last life, I'd gone as far as I could without gambling everything.

about: An old man is testing you to see if you're worthy. He starts things off in a dream and pulls you back from a prison cell every time you die. You work your way through a ruined underground empire and collect the things he carries: staff, amulet, ring, book, hood and cloak, key. Mostly the place rewards decency and patience: you feed a starving old man, greet a sailor, let a crook cheat you and wait for him to come back. Then come the hard mechanical puzzles, a mirror box steered past killer statues and a time machine.

moments.note: The figure among the trees that's always a trunk when you look straight at it.
Shouting up the cliff got the reply 'Pity there's no way of sending it up.' A hint and a taunt at once.
The waiting on the ledge is told through sound alone: a lock tried, a lid opening, coins counted and recounted. It made waiting worth doing.
The man really did pull me up, and he gave me the staff from the dream.
Bread for the old man; he showed me the secret door and vanished.
Taking the staff back out of the beam shut the mirror, so I had to walk all the way to the cliff for the chest.
Bludgeons came through the roof of the box. I had no warning the Guardians were that close.
I couldn't tell what I did wrong in the box. Maybe the open pine panel? Maybe how it was turned?
The lake description warns clearly about what you'll lose, and diving for the amulet worked.
Walking up the side passage next to the box killed me instantly. Nothing hinted that the side passages led past the statues.
With the box parked by the statues, I couldn't find any way back in. I had no panel name to use from outside.
On the third revival the old man is weaker and says there may not be a fourth. A real sense of stakes.
The time machine took everything I was holding.
I heard the guards march off and a great door boom shut, and realized that was the iron door I'd seen rusted in the present.
The jewel room was locked from the inside: 'whoever opens it is meant to be in there already.' Clever, but I had nothing to try.

wished: Some way to tell how the mirror box had to be set up before the Guardians killed me, like a clue from the statues or the box
A way back into the box from outside once it was parked by the Guardians
Taking the sword from the rock, or at least learning what it waits for
To meet whatever made the footsteps in the Land of Shadow
Some warning before the time machine strips everything I was holding

lines.line: Whatever it was, if it was anything, has the knack of being a trunk whenever you look straight at it, and of being a little to one side of where you looked when you look away.
lines.why: It set the uncanny tone and stuck with me.

lines.line: The counting stops, and starts again from the beginning, by somebody who does not trust his own arithmetic.
lines.why: Funny, and it gave me a character I never saw clearly.

lines.line: "Perhaps what you seek is through there!" He points at the carved wall to the north
lines.why: My first clear sign of progress toward the goal.

lines.line: Three times now I have sent you back, my friend, and the power I spend on you is not in endless store; I do not think there is a fourth in me.
lines.why: It turned death from a nuisance into real stakes and changed how carefully I played.

lines.line: The stone door is closed, and locked from the Jewel Room's side; whoever opens it is meant to be in there already.
lines.why: A clever riddle about time, and also where I got stuck.

fun.why: The cliff and chest scene, the old man and the lake dive were all rewarding. The deaths at the Guardians took some of the fun away.

engagement.why: I always had a clear purpose: get to the old man. The dwindling revivals made each choice feel heavy.

difficulty.why: The Guardians kill you with little warning, and once the box was parked I couldn't get back in. The time-machine and jewel-room puzzle gave me nothing to grab onto.

interestingness.why: Using the chest to block the beam, the time machine, and hearing the future's rusted door shut in the past were all inventive.

prose.why: The new prose is excellent: told through sound, wry, and closely observed, especially the waiting on the ledge and the old man's tired speech.
